scene: Alone in an empty warehouse with a cop who is tied to a chair and gagged, a gangster in a black suit saunters around him with breezy swagger, almost dancing, then pulls out a razor and slices off the cop's ear.
song: Stuck in the Middle with You

scene: Two lovers in a diner leap onto their seats and announce a hold-up; the image freezes and bold opening titles slam onto the screen.
In a retro 1950s-themed restaurant, a hitman and his boss's wife kick off their shoes and do a playful, deadpan twist dance on a small stage for a trophy.
Alone in her dim living room, a woman sways sensually to a record while her date argues with himself in the bathroom, moments before she snorts heroin by mistake.
song: Girl, You'll Be a Woman Soon

scene: A crime boss and her sword-carrying bodyguards stride in slow motion through a Tokyo restaurant, a wall of black suits, utterly in control.
A bloodied bride lies on a chapel floor; her former lover tells her this is him at his most masochistic and shoots her in the head. Black-and-white opening credits follow.
song: Bang Bang (My Baby Shot Me Down)

scene: In a snow-covered Japanese garden at night, two women face each other with katanas for a final duel, the fight building to a single fatal stroke.
A flight attendant in a blue uniform glides along an airport moving walkway in profile, cool and unhurried, then hurries to work as the credits roll.
A young woman prepares for revenge on the night of a Nazi film premiere: she applies red lipstick and war-paint rouge, loads a gun, and looks down at the crowd from a window.
A freed man remembers his wife trying to run away from a plantation and being whipped as punishment, the memories intercut with his ride across the snow.

film: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
scene: Dusk in 1969 Los Angeles: one by one, neon signs on movie theaters and diners flicker on while characters drive home, a wistful montage of a city at the end of an era.
A getaway driver in sunglasses waits outside a bank, drumming on the wheel; when his crew bursts out he launches into a screeching, drifting car chase through Atlanta traffic.
In one long take a young man in earbuds bops down a busy city street on a coffee run, his steps landing on the beat as graffiti and passersby seem to sync to him.
A gun deal in a meat warehouse goes wrong and erupts into a shootout, every gunshot landing on the beat like a percussion section.
Trapped in a pub, a group of friends beat a zombie landlord with pool cues in rhythm while the jukebox plays and the lights flash.
A space adventurer in a mask strolls through an abandoned alien ruin, dancing, kicking alien creatures aside and using one as a microphone as the title card appears.
While a team of heroes battles a giant tentacled space monster in the background, a tiny tree creature dances obliviously in the foreground.
After a big heist, the bodies of the crew are discovered one by one: in a car, in a garbage truck, hanging in a meat truck, in slow, mournful tracking shots.
A young gangster takes his date through the back entrance of a nightclub in one long unbroken shot, down stairs and through the kitchen to a table set up just for them.
A paranoid, coke-fuelled day: a gangster races between drug deals and stirring a sauce at home, convinced a helicopter is following him.
A young man in Little Italy wakes from a bad dream, looks in the mirror and lies back down; grainy home movies of friends and a christening play over the titles.
Gritty Boston streets: an undercover cop is pulled deeper into an Irish mob crew, shakedowns and brawls cut together at a rough, brawling pace.
Five friends cram into a beat-up car at night, sing along to a rock opera on the radio, then all headbang together in sync.
With his parents away, a teenager in a shirt, socks and underwear slides across the hardwood floor and dances alone in the living room, singing into a candlestick.
Saturday detention ends; the rebel walks across the empty school football field and punches his fist into the air as the image freezes.
At dawn, a heartbroken young man stands outside his girlfriend's bedroom window holding a boombox high above his head without saying a word.
At a summer resort's end-of-season show, a dance instructor pulls a young woman on stage; they dance, she runs and he lifts her overhead as the whole room joins in.
song: (I've Had) The Time of My Life

scene: Fighter jets launch off an aircraft carrier deck at sunrise in silhouette, deck crews signaling, afterburners roaring.
A boxer who has lost his edge trains to win back his title: sparring, running on the beach, sweating through punishing workouts in a montage.
An investment banker in a raincoat lectures his drunk colleague about a pop band's artistic growth while laying newspapers on the floor, then swings an axe into his head.
Young heroin addicts sprint down an Edinburgh street fleeing store security, one laughing as he's hit by a car, while a voiceover sneers about choosing life.
A man overdoses on heroin and sinks into the red carpet as if into a grave, then is dragged to a taxi and dumped at a hospital.
Dawn in a quiet suburb: a slow montage of people waking alone in their beds, each sensing something they cannot remember, after a boy has died.
A young couple who just fled her wedding sit at the back of a bus, giddy and laughing, until their smiles slowly fade into uncertainty.
Two bikers on chopper motorcycles ride along an open desert highway, free and wild, the landscape rolling past.
A jungle tree line explodes in napalm while helicopters drift through yellow smoke; a soldier lies sweating in a Saigon hotel room, ceiling fan dissolving into rotor blades.
A wounded soldier is chased out of the jungle by enemy troops; from a departing helicopter his comrades watch him fall to his knees, arms raised, as he is shot.
A space shuttle slowly approaches a giant rotating wheel-shaped space station and docks with balletic grace against the stars.
A prisoner locks himself in the warden's office and plays a record over the prison loudspeakers; in the yard every inmate stops and stares upward, transfixed.
A man and a woman hold hands in an empty office tower at night and watch, through the window, as skyscrapers across the city collapse in controlled explosions.
After a bitter fight, a sullen rock band sits in silence on their tour bus; one by one they start singing along to a song on the radio until everyone is smiling.
At a children's beauty pageant, a little girl performs a wildly inappropriate dance routine her grandfather taught her, and her whole family jumps on stage to join her.
In a dim basement lair, a serial killer applies makeup and dances slowly for a video camera in front of a mirror, wrapped in a shawl.
In a crowded Tokyo street, an older man catches up with a young woman, embraces her and whispers something we cannot hear before they part for good.
In a hospital waiting room, a quirky young woman hands a stranger her headphones and tells him a song will change his life; he listens, and something in his face softens.

film: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
scene: A teenage girl stands up in the back of a pickup truck as it speeds through a tunnel at night, arms spread wide in the wind, while her friends watch in awe.
A quiet stunt driver takes his neighbor and her young son for a drive along the Los Angeles river channel at golden hour, glances and small smiles instead of words.
After a tense nighttime getaway, a silent driver cruises the empty neon-lit freeways of Los Angeles as pink script opening credits appear.
A ten-year-old boy runs excitedly through a small German town in 1945 in his youth uniform, intercut with archival footage of adoring crowds at Nazi rallies.
Super-slow-motion carnage in an overrun America: zombies tear through a wedding, a strip club and a fire truck crash as the title fills the screen.
